governing_rules: Repository existence does not create canonical standing.
Where the evidence stops, the claim stops.
Where access stops, public verification stops.
Versions are local to a repository and cannot establish cross-repository precedence.
A pull-request candidate is not a merged main release.

public_surfaces.claim: A bounded local artifact enters a boundary envelope where standing is rebound, admissibility is checked, refusal or review-only posture is emitted, receipts are preserved, replay compares governing conditions, and tamper breaks lineage verification.
public_surfaces.tested_corridor: Repository-local stable release-hash verification and stable proof-suite execution.
public_surfaces.boundary: No production certification, third-party certification, deployed no-bypass proof, customer corridor certification, or protected kernel disclosure.

public_surfaces.claim: Within the bounded demonstrator, only EXECUTE may mutate protected state and every non-EXECUTE outcome must leave protected state unchanged.
public_surfaces.tested_corridor: Repository-local valid execute, invalid authority, stale evidence, degraded visibility, and integrity-failure cases.
public_surfaces.boundary: No production substrate, deployment authorization, open-source license, physical-system validation, or certified safety claim.

public_surfaces.claim: The bounded public harness classifies synthetic AI-assisted financial intent before simulated value-bearing motion and keeps unresolved review, escalation, quarantine, or refusal non-binding.
public_surfaces.tested_corridor: Ten repository-local synthetic financial-motion cases; no settlement execution or payment-rail access.
public_surfaces.boundary: No bank certification, payment-rail certification, statutory compliance, custody-service status, live funds transfer, or production deployment claim.

workflow_or_artifact.expected_result: Reviewer can inspect the bind-time authority, deterministic replay, no-resurrection, and mutation-detectability invariants.

public_surfaces.claim: The public-safe specification defines authority revalidation at the exact boundary where protected consequence would form.
public_surfaces.tested_corridor: Public demonstrator specification and disclosed invariants only; no production cryptography or production authority path is asserted.
public_surfaces.boundary: No production authority evaluator, key-management architecture, signing infrastructure, standing-token format, corridor implementation, or production ledger claim.

workflow_or_artifact.expected_result: Reviewer is routed to exact bounded repositories and their own evidence paths.

public_surfaces.claim: The portfolio provides a human-readable directory of admitted public proof roles and protected reference lineage.
public_surfaces.tested_corridor: Navigation and claim-control only; underlying technical behavior must be verified in the referenced repository.
public_surfaces.boundary: The portfolio is not substitute technical evidence and does not independently establish runtime behavior.

protected_reference_surfaces.refusal_reason: The implementation and workflow evidence are not accessible to an unauthenticated public reviewer.
protected_reference_surfaces.claim: The protected candidate implements bounded software-in-the-loop standing resolution, proof-bound authority, signed consumption attestation, continuity custody, and exactly-once protected consequence commitment.
protected_reference_surfaces.tested_corridor: Declared Python 3.11 and 3.12 private software workflows and negative regressions at the pinned pull-request head.
protected_reference_surfaces.boundary: No physical truth, qualified sensing, certified functional safety, hard real-time guarantee, isolated production gateway, managed KMS/HSM deployment, guarded-workcell validation, independent reproduction, merged main release, or production admission.

withheld_from_canonical_public_proof.reason: The repository states that fresh-clone and CI evidence remain pending; it is not promoted by version number or implementation language alone.

attribution.collaboration_rule: Terry Snyder is attributed only where a repository, document, revision, or proof surface explicitly declares shared lineage, collaboration, or co-development.
